title: How the screening room is built
question: The world is settled — this is composition. The roll led with Mirror and Target. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Mirror and Target
options.lineage: the clinician's mirror held beside the fixation target
options.thesis: You see your own face and the target at once, so you always know you are framed and following correctly.
options.viewport: A muted mirror of your own face on the left, the moving target on the right, a symptom strip waiting below.
options.case: Self-view solves framing and proves adherence — but during a task your eyes belong on the target, not on yourself, so the mirror must recede the moment a task starts.
options.risk: A live picture of your own face is the single most distracting thing you can put next to a fixation target.

options.label: Step Cards
options.lineage: the paper VOMS form, one line at a time
options.thesis: One full screen per step, moving forward only, so there is never more than one thing to hold in mind.
options.viewport: One centered card carrying this step alone, a thin rail marking how far through the seven tasks you are.
options.case: Lowest possible cognitive load per screen, and the closest analogue to the paper instrument clinicians already trust.
options.risk: Seven tasks times instruction, task, and rating is a lot of screens; it can feel like a form rather than a measurement.

options.label: Held Frame
options.lineage: bench instruments — the panel never moves, only the reading does
options.thesis: One screen that never scrolls and never reflows; the chrome is nailed down and only the measurement inside it changes.
options.viewport: A still, dim panel: protocol down the left, the measurement field held dead centre, state down the right — none of it ever moves.
options.case: Motion sensitivity and vestibular symptoms are what the tool measures, so a layout that never moves is the one structure that never provokes what it is trying to observe.
options.risk: Fixed chrome on a small laptop squeezes the centre field, and the stimulus needs real room to travel.
